Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The appellant has filed this regular second appeal challenging the order dated 20.01.2015 passed by the Fast Track Court II and Additional District Judge, Belgaum (hereinafter referred to as the 'first appellate Court') in R.A.No.133/2014, by which an application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 was rejected and consequently the appeal in R.A.No.133/2014 was dismissed.

2. The facts in brief are that respondent No.1 herein filed O.S.No.21/1997 before the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.), Saundatti (hereinafter referred to as the 'trial Court') for declaration of her title in respect of the property bearing Block No.530 measuring 16 acres situated at Madamageri village, Saundatti taluk, Belagavi district.
She claimed that the aforesaid property was NC: 2024:KHC-D:469 granted in favour of her father Yamanappa on 14.08.1959 and his name was entered in the mutation in ME.No.1763.
After his death, she succeeded to the suit property.

She claimed that she had a brother by name Bhimappa (appellant) whose name also appeared in the record of rights but he was not residing in the village and his whereabouts were not known for more than 15 years.
She claimed that Bhimappa (appellant) had no other legal heir and that she was the only legal heir.
She therefore claimed that, she was the absolute owner in exclusive possession of the suit property.
3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit and claimed that 16 acres of land was granted in favour of Mallappa Durgappa Harijan on 19.11.1959 and his name was entered in the mutation as per ME.No.1763.

He claimed that the said Mallappa executed a Will in favour of defendant No.1 as he had no issues and therefore, defendant No.1 was enjoying the entire extent along with his uncle (Mallappa) and that he is now in possession of 5 NC: 2024:KHC-D:469 acres of land.
He contended that none of the plaintiffs had any right, title or interest over the suit property.

Based on these contentions, the trial Court framed following issues:
"1.
Whether plff proves that she is the owner of suit property measuring 16As out of Block No:530 of Madamgeri village?
2. Whether plff is entitled for the relief of injunction sought for?

4. Whether valuation made and court fee paid is proper?
5. Whether plff proves that this court has got pecuniary jurisdiction to try this suit?
6. Whether deft No:1 is entitled for compensatory costs sought for?

7. What order or Decree?"
4.
Respondent No.1 herein was examined as PW3.
Defendant No.1 was examined as DW1 and Exs.P1 to P22 were marked.

Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the trial Court held that respondent No.1 herein was the owner of the suit property and consequently decreed the suit and directed defendant Nos.2 to 4 to demarcate the exact area acquired and to award NC:
2024:KHC-D:469 compensation in favour of respondent No.1.
A decree of injunction was also granted restraining defendant Nos.2 to 4 from disbursing the compensation in favour of defendant No.1.

This judgment was passed on 08.12.2003.
5.
The appellant herein challenged the said judgment and decree in R.A.No.133/2014 and filed an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay in filing the appeal.
6. The first appellate Court recorded the evidence of the appellant on the application and in terms of the impugned order, rejected the application and consequently dismissed R.A.No.133/2014.
Being aggrieved by the same, the appellant has filed this appeal.
7. After hearing the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.1, the following substantial questions of law would arise for consideration:

( i ) Whether the First Appellate Court committed an error in rejecting an application filed by the NC: 2024:KHC-D:469 appellant under Section 5 of the Limitation Act,
1963 unmindful of the averments made in the plaint in O.S.No.21/1997 which indicated that the appellant and respondent No.1 herein were the co- owners of the suit property?

(ii) Was the First Appellate Court justified in misreading the evidence of the appellant, to return a finding that the appellant knew about the judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.21/1997 five years prior to the filing of R.A.No.133/2014?
8.

Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the appellant agreed to sell the suit property to a person named Bhimappa Ramappa Adin on 28.07.2010 and that the said Bhimappa Ramappa Adin filed a suit in O.S.No.245/2013 for specific performance of the agreement of sale.
The said suit was not only filed against the appellant but also filed against respondent No.1 herein.

He contended that respondent No.1 filed a written statement on 17.03.2014 and pleaded in the written statement Bhimappa Yamanappa Harijan @ Talawar vs Rotewwa W/O Bhimappa Hosalli on 9 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83943991/
3 that she was declared as an absolute owner of the suit property by the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.),
Saundatti in O.S.No.21/1997.

sentences.text: He therefore submits that the appellant NC: 2024:KHC-D:469 came to know about the judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.21/1997 on 08.12.2003 and therefore he filed the appeal in R.A.No.133/2014 on 25.07.2014.
He therefore claimed that he filed the appeal soon after coming to know of the judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.21/1997.
He also contends that the appellant was not a party to the suit in O.S.No.21/1997 and therefore, he could not have been attributed with any knowledge of the pendency of the suit.

This apart, he claimed that between respondent No.1 and the appellant there was no conflict of interest as respondent No.1 herself admitted in the plaint filed in O.S.No.21/1997 that the appellant and respondent No.1 were the co-owners of the suit property.
Therefore, he contended the first appellate Court committed an error in rejecting the application filed by the appellant on purely technical grounds.
He therefore submitted that the first appellate Court ought to have determined the case on merits rather than rejecting the application for condonation of delay.

Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 submits that the evidence adduced by the appellant on the application for condonation of delay, in R.A.No.133/2014 indicated beyond doubt that the appellant knew about the suit in O.S.No.21/1997 at least five years prior to filing of the appeal.
He therefore, submits that the first Appellate Court was justified in rejecting the application for condonation of delay.

At any rate, he submits that R.A.No.133/2014 was filed to challenge the judgment and decree passed on 08.12.2003 and therefore, there was enormous delay of more than ten years and hence, the first appellate Court was justified in rejecting the application filed by the appellant for condonation of delay.
10. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.1.
I have also perused the records of the trial Court in O.S.No.21/1997 as well as the records in NC: 2024:KHC-D:469 R.A.No.133/2014 as well as the respective judgments and orders.

11. The first appellate Court rejected the application filed by the appellant for condonation of delay on the ground that the appellant knew about the decree passed in O.S.No.21/1997 at least five years prior to the filing of R.A.No.133/2014.

The first appellate Court failed to notice the following facts before rejecting the application filed by the appellant:
(a) That the appellant was an illiterate person who according to respondent No.1 was not residing in the village and his whereabouts were not known, thereby meaning that he was a nomad.

( b) Respondent No.1 suggested in the course of cross-examination of the appellant on the application for condonation of delay that the appellant was mentally unstable person, thereby making it more than evident that the appellant could not have been treated as a man of prudence.

4 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:469 (c) That the respondent No.1 admitted that the appellant too had an undivided right, title and interest in the suit property and that since his whereabouts were not known, she had become the fully and absolute owner of the suit property.
12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The first appellate Court must have therefore considered the application for condonation of delay more pragmatically having regard to the admitted facts and circumstances of the case.
The appellate Court could not have microscopically examined some evidence extracted from the mouth of the appellant who was not a man of ordinary prudence.

This apart, the claim of the appellant that he came to know about the decree passed in O.S.No.21/1997 only when respondent No.1 filed written statement in O.S.No.245/2013 cannot be totally disbelieved as it could be possible that the appellant came to know of the correct particulars of the litigation filed in O.S.No.21/1997 only after the same was put in writing in the written statement filed in O.S.No.245/2013.

Having regard to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:469 and also having regard to the fact that the dismissal of the appeal would deprive the appellant of valuable right, title and interest which is acknowledged and admitted by respondent No.1 in very many terms in the plaint filed in O.S.No.21/1997
, the impugned order passed by the first appellate Court rejecting the application filed by the appellant for condonation of delay deserves to be set aside.
Consequently, the substantial questions of law framed by this Court are answered in favour of the appellant and against the respondent No.1.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed.
(ii) The impugned order dated 20.01.2015 passed by the Fast Track Court II and Addl. District Judge, Belgaum in R.A.No.133/2014 is set aside.
- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:469 (iii) The application for condonation of delay filed by the appellant is allowed and the delay in filing the appeal is condoned.

(iv) The appeal before the first appellate Court is restored to file and the first appellate Court is directed to dispose off the appeal by taking into consideration the averments made by respondent Bhimappa Yamanappa Harijan @ Talawar vs Rotewwa W/O Bhimappa Hosalli on 9 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83943991/
